packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 17 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification was present in my context)

RUNNING NOTES PER IMAGE (appended as viewed)

image-001.jpg (overview): the spine of a bound book lying on its side, covering removed, showing the backs of the paper gatherings (sprinkled red at the left), four double sewing supports, and - in the five panels between/outside the supports - parchment spine-lining strips still in place. Four of the strips carry script, written so that it reads upright in this photograph (lines run across the spine's length; each strip is c. 10-12 lines tall and only 4-8 letters wide). From left to right:
  strip A (far left, partly under the cover turn-in/dark leather): c. 12 lines, dark and abraded;
  strip B (between supports 1 and 2): c. 11 lines, brown ink;
  strip C (between supports 2 and 3): large red initial at the top (two-line or more, with red horizontal stroke beneath - a red lombard/initial, letter tentatively "G" or "E"), then c. 11 lines;
  strip D (between supports 3 and 4): no script; green ground with small red and green dots/flowers and an orange-brown form at top left - painted decoration (border or miniature fragment, tentative);
  strip E (far right, beyond support 4): c. 10 lines, largest and clearest letters.
 Gothic textualis; same or similar hand on A, B, C, E (tentative). No columns, running titles or glosses can be determined from spine strips. Everything is cut left and right.

image-002.jpg (native tile: strip E, far right):
 image-002 l.1: die mi(n)(?)[..]   ("die" then "mi" with a mark above / "nu"; edge)
 image-002 l.2: [.]ie die(?) ic(?)[.]   (rubbed: "ue di ic"/"ic die ie")
 image-002 l.3: Die sot(?)[.]   (larger D/O-like capital, "Die"/"Oie"; then "sot"/"soe"/"soc" - long s + o + cut letter)
 image-002 l.4: [.]n dagho(?)[.]   ("u daghe"/"n dagho"; smeared)
 image-002 l.5: is ic tot(?)   ("is ic" clear; then "tot"/"ton"/"tor")
 image-002 l.6: [.]ach bit(?)[.]   ("ach"/"ech" with a point or stroke; "bit"/"bin"/"hir")
 image-002 l.7: mo(n)t(?) inn(?)[.]   ("mo" with superscript mark - "mōt"/"mo't"; then minims "mi/inn")
 image-002 l.8: [.]s desen(?)[.]   ("is desel."/"us desen" + a further letter, perhaps tall "t"/"l")
 image-002 l.9: [.]o . ic(?) [..]   ("ho"/"so"/"no" + point + "ic"/"ie" + damaged letter under a pale spot)
 image-002 l.10: [dark, abraded; "th..."/"hi..."] [illegible]

image-003.jpg (native tile: strip D, the painted strip): no script. Grey-green wash ground strewn with small green rings/leaves and red dots (berries/flowers), some white/grey round blobs with dark outlines; at the upper left edge an orange-brown vertical form with a thin dark line descending from it and fine radiating pen lines near it; a small pale mark at about three-quarters height that resembles a "2"/"z"-shaped stroke but which I take as part of the painting, not a letter (tentative). Interpretation (tentative): fragment of a painted ground from a miniature or decorated border. The left side continues under the sewing support.

image-004.jpg (native tile: strip C, with red initial):
 image-004 (rubric, above l.1): [red, cut through at the top edge: bottoms of c. 4 red letters, "nia"/"ma"/"illa"?] [illegible]
 image-004 (initial): large red initial, about 3 lines high, with a red baseline stroke; shape reads as G (or E/C with inner vertical); right part cut by the strip edge. Possibly a second red letter/flourish at its right, cut.
 image-004 l.1: Soo(?)[..]   (first letter a tall form with a top hook: long s or capital L/C; then "oo"/"oe"; cut)
 image-004 l.2: mi(n)(?)[..]   (minims "ini"/"mi" + cut letter with a mark above)
 image-004 l.3: [.]n lic(?)[.]   (blurred: "en lic"/"alsc"/"ulso")
 image-004 l.4: als i(?)[.]   ("als" + a minim; or "ala")
 image-004 l.5: [.]ede(?)[.]   (rubbed: "nede"/"rede"/"tede" + letter)
 image-004 l.6: gemi(?)[.]   ("g" + "emi"/"enn"/"enu")
 image-004 l.7: ons(?) [.]   ("ons"/"ous"/"aus" + cut letter)
 image-004 l.8: [capital, M- or X-like, or "Ic"] h(?)[.]   (very uncertain: reads "M ly"/"X h"/"de ly")
 image-004 l.9: groot(?)   ("groot"/"moet"/"groet" - g/m, r/o, o, o/e, t)
 image-004 l.10: [.]ecta(?)[.]   (dark, abraded: "becta"/"hetta"/"lacra") [illegible]

image-005.jpg (native tile: strip B, between supports 1 and 2), 13 line-fragments:
 image-005 l.1: [tops lost under the turn-in: "...n(?) en(?)"] [illegible]
 image-005 l.2: lic(?) acct(?)[.]   (reads "ucaeer"/"lie acce"/"ticaeci"; c/e/t not separable)
 image-005 l.3: [.]n bouē   ("n"/"u" then "bouē" with macron = boue(n)? fairly clear)
 image-005 l.4: [.]minc(?) d[.]   ("dunc"/"minc"/"nunc" + round letter d/o at edge)
 image-005 l.5: [.] voel(?) a[.]   ("voel"/"vael"/"ooel"; then "a"/"h")
 image-005 l.6: [.]e sijn(?)[.]   ("e" + long s + minims + tall final: "sijn"/"suls"/"siila")
 image-005 l.7: [.]een̄(?) so[.]   (two round letters + n with stroke above: "eeñ"/"ccñ"/"oeñ"; then long s + e/o)
 image-005 l.8: met(?) con(?)[.]   ("met"/"mer"/"inct" + "con"/"ten"/"een")
 image-005 l.9: die du h[.]   ("die"/"dio"; "du" + tall h/b)
 image-005 l.10: dese(?) d[.]   ("d" + long-s ligature + "e"; "dese"/"alste"; then d/o)
 image-005 l.11: [..]sibil(?)[.]   (dark; "dibis"/"sibil"/"ubila")
 image-005 l.12: [.]ne(?) oe(?)[.]   ("hic og"/"inc oe"/"ene oe")
 image-005 l.13: dan(?) il(?)[.]   (abraded; "dan"/"den" + tall strokes)

image-006.jpg (native tile: strip A, far left, half under dark leather/paste, surface cockled and cracked), c. 9-10 line-fragments visible:
 image-006 l.1: [dark; illegible]
 image-006 l.2: [.]rec(?)[.]   ("ureo"/"oireo"/"pireo" - 4-5 letters, last round)
 image-006 l.3: [illegible; cracked]
 image-006 l.4: [.]mal(?)   ("anal"/"mal"/"ind" + tall final)
 image-006 l.5: m(?)[...]   (minim + horizontal damage) [illegible]
 image-006 l.6: [..]eu s(?)   (…"eu"/"en" + long s at edge)
 image-006 l.7: v[..]di(?)   ("vildi"/"wi di"/"viun")
 image-006 l.8: [.]ich(?)[.]   ("uich"/"hich"/"with" + minim)
 image-006 l.9: [dark, abraded] [illegible]
 image-006 l.10-11: [illegible]; near the bottom "k"/"h" + minims(?) [illegible]
 Nothing on this strip is secure.

---------------------------------------------------------------
SUMMARY FOR PACKET 17

Layout survey (observation): one overview (001) of a book spine with the covering gone, and five native tiles (002-006), one per spine-lining strip, taken from right to left (002 = far right strip E, 003 = painted strip D, 004 = strip C with red initial, 005 = strip B, 006 = far left strip A). The strips are in situ, pasted over the backs of the gatherings between the sewing supports; script reads upright in the photographs. Each written strip preserves a vertical slice 4-8 letters wide through 10-13 consecutive lines of one text block; no strip shows a margin with certainty (strip C has blank parchment left of its lines, so it may preserve line beginnings beside a left margin - tentative, the blank could also be the space indented around the initial). Columns: not determinable. Running titles: none visible. Rubric: one red line cut through at the very top of strip C, directly above a large red initial (c. 3 lines high, G/E/C-shaped) - tentative interpretation: a rubricated heading followed by the opening of a new text section. Decoration: strip D is painted (green ground with red and green dots/flowers), no text. No underlining, no glosses seen. Gothic textualis, brown-black ink; vernacular with Dutch-type forms (die, ic, is ic, bouē, die du, dese?) - language judgement tentative given how little survives per line.

Selected spans: the opening under the red initial on strip C (004) as the only heading-like feature, then the clearest strips E (002) and B (005) in full; A (006) attempted, essentially unread; D has no text.

Collected readings (see per-image entries for doubts):
 002 (E): die mi(n).. / .ie die ic. / Die sot. / .n dagho. / is ic tot / .ach bit. / mo(n)t inn. / .s desen. / .o . ic .. / ...
 004 (C): [red rubric, cut] / [red initial G?] / Soo.. / mi(n).. / .n lic. / als i. / .ede. / gemi. / ons . / M? h. / groot? / .ecta.
 005 (B): ... / lic acct. / .n bouē / .minc d. / . voel a. / .e sijn. / .een̄ so. / met con. / die du h. / dese d. / ..sibil. / .ne oe. / dan il.
 006 (A): not securely read.

Limitations: each line is represented by at most 4-8 letters, so word identity is mostly a guess and a later source match will need to rely on the vertical sequences on strips E and B and on the rubric + initial on strip C. The strips are transparentised by paste and lie over the paper spine folds, so paper-fold lines and red edge-sprinkling interfere with the letters. The parts of each strip that pass under the sewing supports and under the cover turn-ins are hidden. The relative order of the strips within the original leaf (or leaves) is unknown; they need not be adjacent or from one leaf. Suggested further imaging: transmitted/raking light on strips A and B; a tile of the top of strip C at higher magnification for the red rubric; a view of the other end of the spine if it also carries strips.

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification. I read packet-15 and packet-16 (detached strips in a similar hand and language) earlier in this same session; no identification arose from them. I did not search or consult anything, and opened only PROMPT.md and the packet images (packet.json not opened).
This is an unverified image reading.
